feature: WebTransport HTTP/2 reconnecting State lock admission

behavior.deadline: initial State admission and current/handle lookups use the original awake-clock deadline via the shared timed_mutex helper
behavior.activity: callers register activity before State admission; Timeout/Canceled and ordinary exit release it without reacquiring the mutex
behavior.shutdown: exit notification precedes the final count drop; State destruction waits for registered calls, including contended admission, and cannot race an in-progress notifier
behavior.idle_wait: only shutdown uses a bounded one-millisecond Event wait to resolve a notification preceding the final count drop; normal operation admission and activity release do not poll

python_interop_debug.scope: direct Session wire compatibility with independent Python peer; reconnecting facade integration is covered by the module TLS tests

regressions: 17 public entry points under a held State mutex return Timeout or Canceled without connector calls, generation mutation, connecting changes or retained activity
expired and wrong-clock calls across those entry points return Timeout without even waiting for the State mutex
after successful activity registration, contended current and handle lookups honor deadlines; leave returns activity to zero while the State mutex remains held
shutdown parks while one call remains active; a blocked exit notifier preserves that activity and prevents State destruction; after notification completes shutdown releases State

limitations: this capture proves facade State admission/lookups and activity release; connector callbacks, endpoint worker admission and connect-result/retirement publication have separate lifecycle boundaries
the full protocol-library goal still needs broader integration and long-duration/high-concurrency evidence
